bullets: Drainage is the most crucial design decision for any trail, as ignoring it leads to needing a complete rebuild within a year.
Beginner trail builders commonly make the mistake of digging with too steep a slope, which undermines trail longevity and stability.
Benches along the hillside are not optional — their absence results in erosion that turns the shortcut of year one into a ravine by year three.
Soil erosion and trail construction intersect fundamentally at the design phase, where land management discussions must occur before any ground is disturbed.
The structure of the soil is more important than people realize, and its properties directly influence trail durability and maintenance needs.
Teams using Spoke & Wrench or the Cascadia Alliance reveal trade-offs that are invisible without structured workflows and repeatable processes.
Machine-made trails are not inherently better than hand-built ones — the method matters less than the design integrity and adherence to ecological principles.
Failure modes are difficult to identify outside of established frameworks like the Cascadia Alliance, where structural aspects and second-order effects are often overlooked.
